canonical_question: How does the 'inhomogeneity of the subgrain structure' specifically manifest in the diffraction data compared to simple intergranular strain variations?

question_variants.question: How does the 'inhomogeneity of the subgrain structure' specifically manifest in the diffraction data compared to simple intergranular strain variations?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text asserts that inhomogeneity of the subgrain structure is usually more related to the accumulation of dislocations than to variations of intergranular strains, distinguishing the two manifestations.

answers.answer: Inhomogeneity of the subgrain structure manifests in diffraction data as being more related to the accumulation of dislocations than to variations of intergranular strains.
answers.boundary_limitation: Comparison is qualitative ('more related to'); specific diffraction signatures distinguishing the two are not detailed in the provided span.
evidence_spans: The microstructure of the homogenized NbTaTiV refractory HEA was characterized, using the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) backscattered electron (BSE) technique, as shown in Fig. 1A . A typical simple solid-solution HEA microstructure with grain sizes of 200 to 400 μm was identified without the presence of secondary phases or elemental segregations.

The chemical composition of the sample was verified (using the point energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis) to be Nb 23.8 Ta 25.5 Ti 24.9 V 25.8 , indicating a homogeneous elemental distribution in a nearly equiatomic percentage.
The measured ND patterns of the bulk samples, as illustrated in Fig. 1B , confirm the single BCC solid solution at RT and elevated temperatures.
